position: Current Regulations That Should Be Rolled Back (Civil Rights Data Collection)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department rescind the Biden-era changes to the Civil Rights Data Collection that added a nonbinary sex category and retired data on high school single-sex athletics sports, teams and participants. It also recommends issuing a new CRDC that collects data directly relevant to the Office for Civil Rights' statutory enforcement authority.

status_summary: ED submitted a revised Civil Rights Data Collection for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 school years to OMB, with a 30-day notice published 2025-08-07 (comments closed 2025-09-08). OMB's reginfo.gov record shows the revision (OMB control number 1870-0504) approved with change on 2026-07-20, with an expiration of 2029-07-31. According to K-12 Dive on 2026-07-31, the approved collection drops the nonbinary category, so schools report students as male or female, and removes gender identity from the rape and sexual assault definitions, with ED citing costs outweighing benefits and Executive Order 14168; NPR reported on 2026-09-04 that the delayed 2023-24 data release omitted nonbinary information and that ED had begun collecting data for the next cycles. Whether the single-sex athletics items are in the approved collection was not confirmed, and no ED statement tying the collection to OCR's statutory enforcement authority was located; the stage rests on the removal of the nonbinary category, which is the change the text names.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14168 was signed, setting a federal policy of recognizing two sexes, male and female; ED later cited it in explaining the CRDC changes, per K-12 Dive.

ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act 30-day notice submitting a revised CRDC (OMB control number 1870-0504, docket ED-2024-SCC-0128) for the 2025-26 and 2027-28 collections; comments closed 2025-09-08.
K-12 Dive reported that the proposal would stop collecting data on nonbinary and transgender students and remove gender identity from the rape definition, as aligned with the 2020 Title IX rule.
OMB concluded its review of the revised CRDC information collection as approved with change, with an expiration date of 2029-07-31.
timeline.source: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (reginfo.gov)

timeline.event: K-12 Dive reported that the approved 2025-26 collection drops the nonbinary category and gender identity wording in the rape and sexual assault definitions, and that districts that had recorded nonbinary students must recode them as male or female.

NPR reported that the 2023-24 CRDC data released by ED omitted information on nonbinary students, that the 2025-26 collection eliminates the nonbinary category, and that a department spokesperson confirmed data collection for the next cycles had begun.

title: Drop the CRDC nonbinary category, keep athletics data, refocus CRDC on OCR enforcement
uncertainties: The Federal Register notice of 2025-08-07 (re-read in the second review) and the reginfo.gov ICR page do not list individual data elements; the notice abstract says only that ED will refine, add or remove elements and points to the supporting statement and attachments. The specific changes (nonbinary category, rape and sexual assault definitions, LGBTQ harassment items) come from K-12 Dive and NPR reporting and from a multistate attorneys general comment letter on the proposal (oag.ca.gov); the supporting statement and the comment response on reginfo.gov could not be opened, and the ED CRDC page on ed.gov returned an error. No source read mentions athletics in the 2025-26 proposal or approval: K-12 Dive and NPR are silent on it. A vendor help page (kb.infinitecampus.com) shows single-sex athletics questions in the 2021-22 collection, which suggests the retirement the Mandate objected to may not have taken effect, but this was not confirmed from ED documents. The Mandate refers to the December 2021 notice for the 2021-22 collection.
